Let \(v(a)\) denote the \(p\)-adic valuation of a residue modulo \(p^n\), with \(v(0)=n\). Write \(a=v(x)\), \(b=v(y)\).

If \(2a\ge n\) and \(3b\ge n\), then both sides are \(0\pmod {p^n}\). The number of such pairs is
\[
p^{n-\lceil n/2\rceil}\,p^{n-\lceil n/3\rceil}
=
p^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lfloor 2n/3\rfloor}.
\]

Otherwise both sides are nonzero modulo \(p^n\), so their valuations must be equal:
\[
2a=3b<n.
\]
Thus \(a=3r,\ b=2r\), with \(6r<n\). Put \(m=n-6r\). Then
\[
x=p^{3r}X,\qquad y=p^{2r}Y
\]
with \(X,Y\) units, and the equation becomes
\[
X^2\equiv Y^3\pmod {p^m}.
\]

Now count unit solutions modulo \(p^m\). In the unit group \(G=(\mathbb Z/p^m\mathbb Z)^\times\), the equation is
\[
U^2=V^3.
\]
The map
\[
W\mapsto (W^3,W^2)
\]
is a bijection from \(G\) to the solution set: if \(U^2=V^3\), then \(W=V^2U^{-1}\) gives \(W^2=V\) and \(W^3=U\). Hence there are
\[
|G|=\varphi(p^m)=p^{m-1}(p-1)
\]
unit solutions modulo \(p^m\).

For fixed \(r\), each unit \(U\bmod p^m\) lifts to \(p^{3r}\) possible \(X\bmod p^{n-3r}\), and each \(V\bmod p^m\) lifts to \(p^{4r}\) possible \(Y\bmod p^{n-2r}\). Therefore the contribution for this \(r\) is
\[
p^{3r}p^{4r}\varphi(p^{n-6r})
=
p^{7r}p^{n-6r-1}(p-1)
=
(p-1)p^{n+r-1}.
\]

Summing over
\[
0\le r\le \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{6}\right\rfloor
\]
gives
\[
\sum_{r=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/6\rfloor}(p-1)p^{n+r-1}
=
p^{n-1}\left(p^{\lfloor (n-1)/6\rfloor+1}-1\right).
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{
N_n(p)=p^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+\lfloor 2n/3\rfloor}
+
p^{n-1}\left(p^{\lfloor (n-1)/6\rfloor+1}-1\right)
}.
\]

This also checks at \(n=1\): the formula gives \(1+(p-1)=p\), corresponding to \((0,0)\) and the \(p-1\) unit parametrizations \((t^3,t^2)\).
